Name: Overflow XP
Author: MarsXsyper
Description:
[color=#fafafa][size=4][b]Description[/b][/size][/color]
Redistributes XP between eligible vanilla and SpaceCore skills, with optional sharing between multiplayer characters, multiple distribution modes, Percentage, Multiply and Equal options, and Mastery integration.

[color=#fafafa][size=4][b]Main Features[/b][/size][/color]
[list]
[*]Supports all five vanilla skills.[/*]
[*]Supports SpaceCore custom skills.[/*]
[*]Detects each skill’s individual maximum level.[/*]
[*]Optional XP sharing between multiplayer characters.[/*]
[*]Supports vanilla Mastery XP.[/*]
[*]Optional SpaceCore skill contribution to Mastery.[/*]
[*]Configurable sharing with locked custom skills.[/*]
[*]Preserves unused XP as Pending when applicable.[/*]
[*]Optional [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] integration.[/*]
[/list][heading]Distribution Modes[/heading]
[list]
[*][b]Even Distribution[/b]
Shared XP is divided as evenly as possible between all eligible destination skills, respecting their remaining capacity.[/*]
[*][b]Lowest XP First[/b]
Prioritizes the eligible destination with the lowest current XP.When that skill reaches its maximum, any remaining shared XP continues to the next eligible destination within the same event. Destination skills with 0 XP are ignored by this mode.[/*]
[*][b]Highest XP First[/b]
Prioritizes the eligible destination with the highest current XP that hasn’t reached its maximum.When that skill reaches its maximum, any remaining shared XP continues to the next eligible destination within the same event.[/*]
[*][color=#fafafa][b]Overly Distributed XP[/b][/color]
Overly Distributed XP is now an independent option.Enabling it allows skills to share XP before reaching their maximum level. It preserves your selected Distribution Mode and Experience Amount settings.For example, you can combine it with:[/*]
[*]Lowest XP First + Percentage.[/*]
[*]Highest XP First + Multiply.[/*]
[*]Even Distribution + Equal.
Disabling it restores the normal maximum-level sharing requirement.This option does not allow below-max source skills to contribute to Mastery.[/*]
[/list][heading]Experience Amount[/heading]
Choose from [b]10%–90%[/b], [b]Multiply[/b], or [b]Equal[/b]. The default is [b]60%[/b].

[b]Percentage
[/b]The selected percentage remains in the primary channel, while the rest is shared.
For example, with [b]60%[/b]:
[list]
[*][b]100 XP earned[/b][/*]
[*][b]60 XP → source skill or eligible source Mastery[/b][/*]
[*][b]40 XP → selected destination skills[/b][/*]
[/list]When the source cannot use its primary portion, that XP becomes available for redistribution.

[b]Multiply[/b]
Multiply creates a full copy of the original XP for each [b]selected destination[/b].
For example, with Even Distribution:
[list]
[*][b]10 XP earned[/b][/*]
[*][b]4 eligible destination skills[/b][/*]
[*][b]Each destination receives up to 10 XP[/b][/*]
[/list]With Lowest XP First or Highest XP First, Multiply copies XP to the destination selected by that mode.
Each copy respects the destination’s maximum. Unused portions of copies are discarded instead of becoming Pending.
Multiply can greatly accelerate progression, especially with [b]Overly Distributed XP[/b] enabled.

[b]Equal[/b]
Equal divides XP equally between the [b]origin channel and selected destinations[/b], instead of reserving a fixed percentage for the origin.
For example:
[list]
[*][b]100 XP earned[/b][/*]
[*][b]1 available origin channel + 4 destination skills[/b][/*]
[*][b]Each channel receives 20 XP[/b][/*]
[/list]If the source is already at its maximum, its origin channel can use eligible Mastery instead. If neither the source skill nor its Mastery can receive XP, that channel is excluded.
Equal divides the current XP amount; it does [b]not[/b] equalize the skills’ accumulated XP.
With Lowest XP First or Highest XP First, the origin and current priority destination receive equal portions. Distribution continues when a destination reaches its maximum.
Enable [b]Overly Distributed XP[/b] to use Equal sharing before the source reaches its maximum.

[heading]Multiplayer XP Sharing[/heading]
Enable [b]Share XP with Other Players[/b] to include eligible skills belonging to connected participants in the same distribution pool as your own skills.
The selected distribution and amount settings apply across that pool:
[list]
[*][b]Even Distribution:[/b] divides shared XP across eligible destinations.[/*]
[*][b]Lowest/Highest XP First:[/b] prioritizes skills across participating characters.[/*]
[*][b]Multiply:[/b] creates copies for selected destinations.[/*]
[*][b]Equal:[/b] includes the source’s origin channel in the division.[/*]
[/list]Another character’s copy of the source skill can receive shared XP.
Each participating player needs [b]Overflow XP 1.1.0 or later[/b]. Players without a compatible version are excluded from sharing.
XP, Pending and Mastery are handled separately for each character. Received shared XP does not trigger another sharing cascade.
Player sharing is [b]enabled by default[/b]. Disabling it stops sending and receiving shared XP for that instance while preserving sharing among your own skills. 

[heading]Pending XP[/heading]
Percentage and Equal preserve XP that cannot currently be allocated, including applicable rounding remainders.
Pending can be released by the next normal XP gain [b]without requiring fresh overflow[/b].
Lowest XP First and Highest XP First now continue through eligible destinations immediately when a selected skill reaches its maximum, instead of leaving usable XP waiting in Pending.
Multiply does not create Pending from unused copies and does not multiply or erase an existing Pending balance.
Pending is saved separately for each character.
[heading]Mastery[/heading]
Vanilla source skills at their maximum can contribute to Stardew Valley’s Mastery system while Mastery is still available.
SpaceCore source skills can also contribute when:
[b]SpaceCore Skills Share with Mastery = Enabled[/b]
This option is [b]disabled by default[/b].
Mastery is awarded to the character who earned the source XP. Other players’ Mastery is not included as a shared destination.
[heading]Locked Skills[/heading]
By default, locked custom skills cannot receive shared XP.
Some SpaceCore skills have specific unlock conditions, so Overflow XP does not simply treat [b]level 0[/b] as meaning a skill is locked.
For multiplayer sharing with a locked destination, both the sender and recipient must allow locked-skill sharing.
[heading]Generic Mod Config Menu[/heading]
If [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] is installed, Overflow XP can be configured directly in-game.
Available settings:
[list]
[*][b]Distribution Mode[/b][/*]
[*][b]Experience Amount[/b][/*]
[*][b]Overly Distributed XP[/b][/*]
[*][b]Share XP with Other Players[/b][/*]
[*][b]Share XP with Locked Skills[/b][/*]
[*][b]SpaceCore Skills Share with Mastery[/b][/*]
[/list]GMCM is optional. All settings are also available through
[code]config.json[/code][size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]SMAPI 4.0.0+[/color]
[color=#D4D4D8]
[b][size=4]Installation instructions[/size][/b][/color]

[list=1]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Install SMAPI.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Download Overflow XP.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Extract the Overflow XP folder into:[/color][/*]
[/list][color=#D4D4D8]Stardew Valley/Mods/

The result should look like:
Mods/
└─ Overflow XP/
  ├─ OverflowXP.dll
  └─ manifest.json[/color]
